fieldMarks: Flanks sharply barred black and white; back feathers edged warm buff; much reddish on the wings.
More richly coloured than the clapper rail.
behavior: Call is a harsh, clattering kek-kek-kek, almost identical to the clapper rail's.
Forages in shallow water near dense cover; carries large prey such as crayfish to solid ground.
Eats aquatic insects, crayfish, crabs, small fish, snails, frogs and seeds.
Withdraws from northern areas in winter; apparently migrates at night.
habitat: Fresh and brackish marshes, rice fields and swamps with dense cattail, bulrush or spartina; occasionally salt marsh in winter.
range: Eastern North America: eastern Canada and the Great Lakes through New England, the Mid-Atlantic, the Plains and the Southeast to Florida and Texas; withdraws from northern areas in winter.

lookalikes.name: Clapper rail
lookalikes.howToTell: King rail is more richly coloured with sharper black-and-white flank bars; its voice is nearly identical.

lookalikes.name: Virginia rail
lookalikes.howToTell: Virginia rail is much smaller and has gray cheeks.
